about: The answer to the one-line request of exercise 1, shown to participants as the starting point.

issues: It promises the full credit she asked for. Only the {managerRole} can approve a credit of this size, and no credit may be promised by e-mail before it is approved (policy, rules 3 and 6).
It promises to pay for the cups she bought at the cash-and-carry. The policy does not allow that without the {managerRole}'s agreement in writing (rules 5 and 6).
It promises delivery tomorrow. No day has been confirmed, and {staffFirst} wrote that the van does not come to her area until next week (message 4).
It offers a discount that exists nowhere in the thread or the policy.
It does not answer what she is most upset about: {staffFirst} said he would confirm a delivery day by Friday, and did not (messages 4 and 5).
It is long and padded with stock phrases. She asked two plain questions; the reply gives her promises the company may not be able to keep.
